Volvo Car to Cut 2,500 Jobs as Part of Plan to Cut Costs Further
By Dominic Chopping
STOCKHOLM--Volvo Car will cut 2,500 jobs globally as part of an additional turnaround plan that targets over $500 million in cost savings.

The Swedish car maker--which is majority-owned by China's Zhejiang Geely Holding Group--said Friday that the operating environment remains tough, with strong external challenges, and while the long-term strategy is on point, more needs to be done in the short term.

"With severely challenged volumes, we need to reinforce our turnaround plan with additional decisive actions, lowering our break-even point and improving cash flows to make us more resilient," Chief Executive Hakan Samuelsson said.

The company plans to reduce costs by 5 billion Swedish kronor ($504.5 million) on top of earlier cost saving measures, through the job cuts, of which 2,000 are based in Sweden, mainly through ending consultant contracts, natural attrition and targeted exit packages to employees.
Full financial effects of these measures will be realized by the end of 2027, when the company's overall indirect spending will be almost 25% below 2024 levels, it added.
